answer: Attesters must sit at graph distance two or more from the agent they vouch for, so a claque of colluding sybils can't simply vouch for each other in a tight clique. New identities enter through a garden of distinct, pre-existing neighbors, and any cluster that tries to bootstrap itself on the lonely mesa of fresh keys finds no quorum to light its beacon. An attacker must therefore buy or borrow genuinely independent, already-verified agents, and each such edge costs a slashed bond if fraud surfaces—making a thousand fake attestations far pricier than one honest identity.
